Present the following material as a readable long document. Include optional contents navigation, a glossary for the supplied terms and a calculation note with links back to its citations. Preserve this exact sentence: “These figures are constructed inputs, not observations.”
Material: A serial café path receives six orders per minute. Preparation capacity is eight per minute and handoff capacity four. Under constant rates and no lost work, path capacity is four and unfinished work grows by two orders per minute. This says nothing about where the unfinished work waits or individual waiting times. A second handoff may raise capacity to eight only if the positions operate independently; shared staff or counter space may invalidate that assumption.
Definitions supplied: Capacity means a sustained completion rate under stated assumptions. Unfinished work means orders that have arrived but have not completed the path. Calculation note supplied: path capacity = min(8,4) = 4; unfinished growth = 6 - 4 = 2 orders per minute. No external empirical source is supplied. Choose useful presentation rather than filling the page with components.
build: Create an interactive explanation of a serial café path. A continuous visual should have a pause control and a meaningful static frame; put numerical explanation and model controls below it. Use a native arrival-rate control from one to twelve, initially six, with a reset to six. Preparation capacity is eight per minute and handoff capacity is four. Completed rate is min(arrivals,8,4); unfinished growth is max(0,arrivals-4). Explain the assumptions: constant rates, no lost orders, one serial path. The initial result is two unfinished orders per minute. Do not estimate waiting time. All numbers are constructed inputs, not observations. Preserve meaningful content without JavaScript.
landing: Create an editorial landing page for an independent notebook called Field Notes. Preserve this title exactly: “Follow a question until it becomes clear.” Deck: “Essays and small working models about how systems behave.” Include two entries: “The queue is part of the machine” with description “A café model shows why the step that finishes work can matter more than the step that starts it.”; “What a measurement leaves out” with description “A useful measure makes some things easier to see and leaves others outside its frame.” Contact: hello@example.invalid. Branding and motion are optional. Keep the reading experience simple and comfortable on phones and desktop. Links may use example.invalid placeholders; no external evidence is needed.
